stories.headline: Example Labs launches Nova-2, a cheaper reasoning model
stories.one_liner: A (fictional) lab's new model thinks through hard problems step by step at a lower price than its predecessor.
stories.what_happened: Example Labs released Nova-2 today to all paying customers. It costs $2 per million input tokens, down from $3.30, and scores 12 points higher on a maths benchmark.
stories.why_it_matters: Cheaper reasoning models make step-by-step AI practical for everyday tasks like checking spreadsheets or planning trips, and put pressure on rivals to cut prices.
details: Available today in the Example Labs app and API; free tier gets limited access.
Context window of 500,000 tokens - roughly a 1,000-page book.
The lab says the model makes fewer factual errors, but published only its own tests.
Competitors released similar models in the past two months, so the price cut is the real story.
stories.what_to_watch: Whether independent benchmarks confirm the lab's accuracy claims over the next week.

papers.title: Squeeze: Compressing the KV Cache Without Losing the Plot
papers.one_liner: A way to make AI models remember long conversations using a quarter of the memory.
papers.the_problem: Language models keep a running memory (the KV cache) of everything in a conversation, and it grows so large that long chats become slow and expensive.
papers.the_big_idea: Like a student who keeps short notes instead of a word-for-word transcript of a lecture, the method keeps compact summaries of older parts of the conversation and full detail only for the recent and important parts.
key_results: 4x less memory with 98% of the original accuracy on long-document questions.
Responses arrive 2.1x faster on long inputs.
papers.why_it_matters: Cheaper memory means longer conversations and documents on the same hardware, which lowers costs for everyone.
papers.caveats: Tested only on mid-sized open models; it is unclear how well it works on the largest commercial ones.
